title: Survey of DNA polymerase activity during the early development of Drosophila melanogaster.
abstract: The pattern of DNA polymerase activity in developing Drosophila melanogaster has been studied in seven stages of embryonic development as well as in unfertilized eggs. The crude polymerase-containing extracts, most likely of cytoplasmic origin, utilize, in the following order of decreasing template efficiency, "activated" calfthymus DNA, poly(A).oligo(dT), and poly(A).oligo(U). The highest enzymes levels occur in unfertilized eggs; the activity remains high during the first 9 hr of embryogenesis, but shows a progressive decline in the later stages. Deoxyribonuclease exhibits a similar trend. The unfertilized eggs of two genotypically different females had nearly identical levels of DNA polymerase.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
